subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw expose Gateway receive time as agent-visible inbound metadata, and if so what field name, timestamp type, and propagation boundary should become the contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding a prompt-visible metadata field affects plugin/channel contracts, prompt cache volatility, and long-term observability semantics.

options.title: Add canonical receive metadata
options.body: Expose one generic field such as gatewayReceivedAt or gatewayReceivedAtMs through inbound context and agent metadata, with docs and tests covering channel and metadata propagation.

options.title: Keep it diagnostic-only
options.body: Limit receive-time data to logs, telemetry, or internal trace state and close this as not planned for agent-visible metadata.

options.title: Design broader lifecycle timing
options.body: Define a staged timing contract that covers gateway receipt, dispatch start, agent start, first token, and outbound send instead of adding only one metadata field.

recommendation.title: Add canonical receive metadata
recommendation.body: Expose one generic field such as gatewayReceivedAt or gatewayReceivedAtMs through inbound context and agent metadata, with docs and tests covering channel and metadata propagation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current inbound metadata and prompt-cache surface history points most strongly to this owner for the API/product boundary choice.
